Yes — very likely.

At 21.1° altitude, the Moon is comfortably above the horizon, though still fairly low in the southwest (azimuth about 239°, roughly west-southwest). With a clear nighttime sky and the Sun nearly 50° below the horizon, the sky should be dark enough for it to stand out easily.

A 37%-illuminated Moon is a noticeable crescent/gibbous-looking partial Moon and is ordinarily very easy to see with unaided eyes, especially in clear conditions. Its 75° separation from the Sun also means it is well away from any twilight glow.

Look toward the west-southwest, about two fist-widths at arm’s length above the horizon (roughly 20°). Avoid nearby buildings, hills, or haze near the horizon, and it should be plainly visible.
